core_obligations: Transport the over-s' part: apply the base change lemma for one step devissages to the data (Z, Y, i, pi, G) and the affine S' to obtain that (Z', Y', i', pi', G') is a one step devissage of F'/X'/S' over s' (proof lines 942-945).

Upgrade it to a one step devissage at the chosen closed point: verify conditions (1)-(4) of the at-a-point definition for (Z', Y', i', pi', G', z', y'), using the hypothesis kappa(s) = kappa(s') together with the uniqueness of the points x', z', y' lying over both x, z, y and s' to identify the fibres X'_{s'}, Z'_{s'}, Y'_{s'} with X_s, Z_s, Y_s (proof lines 945-950).
proof_roadmap: Apply the over-s' base change lemma of the same chapter to get a one step devissage (Z', Y', i', pi', G') of F'/X'/S' over s' (proof lines 942-945).

Conditions (1)-(4) of the at-a-point definition are unaffected because the residue-field hypothesis makes each primed fibre isomorphic to the corresponding unprimed fibre under the base change map (proof lines 945-950).
difficulty_reason: The statement is the pointed refinement of the base change lemma for one step devissages: the primed data must realise a one step devissage of F'/X'/S' at the specific closed point x' over x, not merely over the base point (statement lines 930-938). The whole substance is that the extra hypothesis kappa(s) = kappa(s') makes the base change maps induce isomorphisms X'_{s'} = X_s, Z'_{s'} = Z_s and Y'_{s'} = Y_s, which is exactly what conditions (1)-(4) of the at-a-point definition test; without the residue-field hypothesis this transport fails (proof lines 945-950). The author carries the whole argument in five lines by quoting the over-s' lemma and the definition, so the difficulty is the localisation bookkeeping and not a new construction: H2.
